answer.reason: The verses give two distinct deeds of Tiglath-pileser beyond the summary: conquering northern Israelite lands and carrying off captives, and answering Ahaz's appeal; the killing of Rezin is already in the summary.

clauses.english: took Galilee, Gilead and the land of Naphtali and carried the people captive to Assyria
clauses.quote: took Ijon, and Abelbethmaachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee

clauses.english: went up against Damascus and took it, answering Ahaz's call for help
clauses.quote: the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, and took it

clauses.english: carried the Reubenites, Gadites and half tribe of Manasseh away to Halah and Habor
clauses.quote: he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh

doubts: 1CH 5:6 and 1CH 5:26 spell the name Tilgathpilneser and 2CH 28:20 Tilgathpilneser; taken as the same king. 1CH 5:26 also names Pul, left out as a possibly separate record.
ISA 7:17 speaks only of the king of Assyria unnamed, so left out.
2CH 28:20-21 says he distressed Ahaz and did not help him, which is not clearly a deed apart from 2KI 16:9, so left out.
